findings.issue: Kana contains extra syllables きごう between です and だから. This is a tokenizer artifact: the removed sentence-break punctuation was read as 記号 (kigou, 'symbol') and leaked into the phonetic transcription. The sentence has no such sounds.
findings.current: もうおそいですきごうだからかえります
findings.suggested: もうおそいですだからかえります

findings.issue: Romaji inherits the phantom 'kigou' (記号, the tokenizer's reading of the removed punctuation). Not covered by the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue — these are extra syllables that do not exist in the sentence.

tokens[3] has surface " " (a space) with reading きごう — a phantom token created when the sentence-break punctuation was glossed as 記号 ('symbol'). It is the root cause of the corrupted kana/romaji and should be deleted entirely.
findings.suggested: (delete this phantom token; a whitespace token has no reading)

findings.issue: Gloss 'to pickle' fits another sense of 漬ける but not this sentence (soaking a shirt in water). The pt gloss 'pôr de molho' is correct; the en gloss should match the in-context sense.

Register mismatch: 〜てください is a polite request, but 'diz' is the informal tu-imperative. Course convention maps polite JP to neutral-polite pt, so the você-form imperative 'diga' is expected (as in lit_pt 'diga').

The English explanation says "the Portuguese 'I can't find'" while quoting English text — a translation artifact from expl_pt (which correctly says "o português 'não consigo achar'"). Should reference the English rendering.
findings.current: so the Portuguese 'I can't find' sounds more natural than the literal 'it isn't found'
findings.suggested: so the English 'I can't find' sounds more natural than the literal 'it isn't found'

findings.issue: Awkward, redundant word order: 'since this morning today' stacks two time expressions unnaturally. 今日は is the topic and should lead.
findings.current: It's been nice since this morning today.
findings.suggested: Today it's been nice out since morning.

findings.issue: Dangling cross-reference: 'Note the contrast with the previous sentence' (also in expl_pt 'a frase anterior') refers to context that does not exist in this standalone record of the sentence bank. The grammar fact itself (な adnominal vs に adverbial) is correct.
findings.current: Note the contrast with the previous sentence: before a noun な is used; in adverbial position に is used.
findings.suggested: Contrast: before a noun, 丁寧 takes な; in adverbial position it takes に (丁寧に).
